Chapter 9: Lessons in Leadership—What the World Can Learn
When you look back, it’s easy to think of the partnership between Angela Merkel and Barack Obama as one of those rare moments in history—two leaders, brought together by the world’s challenges, who somehow managed to achieve something remarkable.
But here’s the thing: the real lesson isn’t just about their personalities or their politics. It’s about the core qualities that make true leadership possible, even when the going gets tough.
Over the years, Merkel and Obama showed us the power of listening—not just hearing, but really listening—to people who see the world differently. They didn’t build trust through dramatic speeches or big promises. Instead, it happened in small ways, through respect and honesty, day after day.
And you know what? They proved that having different opinions isn’t a weakness. In fact, those differences can actually make a team stronger.
There’s this story from the early days of their partnership that really captures what made them special. During a tense negotiation, one of Merkel’s aides got frustrated, thinking the Americans were being totally unreasonable. Merkel quietly pulled her colleague aside and said, “Let’s try to see it from their point of view.” Simple, right? But it completely changed the atmosphere in the room. The Americans picked up on it, and the conversation shifted. That small moment led to a breakthrough that might never have happened otherwise.
Most people forget how important humility is when it comes to leadership. Merkel and Obama weren’t afraid to admit when they were wrong, or to change their minds. They learned from each other, over and over again. For them, leadership wasn’t about knowing everything. It was about asking the right questions and being willing to grow.
Their partnership also showed us the power of resilience—the ability to keep going, even when everything feels impossible. There were times when both of them felt overwhelmed, when the problems just seemed too big. But they didn’t quit. They kept talking. They kept listening. And they never stopped trying.
